context: Adam opens a savings account when he is a certain age and wants a given amount of rand by the time he reaches a later age. The account pays simple interest at a rate that is a whole percent plus one half, per annum.

params.name: ds
params.let: fixed(th / 1000, 3) if th % 10 != 0 else (fixed(th / 1000, 2) if th % 100 != 0 else fixed(th / 1000, 1))

params.why: the principal is not already a whole number of rand, so the rounding step is real
the principal never lies exactly half a cent from a cent, so the rounding is unambiguous

stem: Adam opens a savings account when he is ${=a1}$ years old. He would like to have $\text{R{=A}}$ by the time he is ${=a2}$ years old. If the savings account offers simple interest at a rate of ${=w}.5$ % per annum, how much money should he invest now to reach his goal? Give your answer in rand, correct to two decimal places.
solution: Work out how many years the money is invested: $n={=a2}-{=a1}={=g}$ years.
Write down the simple interest formula: $A=P(1+in)$
Substitute the given values and work out the bracket: $\begin{aligned}\text{R{=A}}&=P\left(1+0.0{=w}5\times{=g}\right)\\\text{R{=A}}&=P\times{=ds}\end{aligned}$
Divide both sides by ${=ds}$ to find $P$: $P=\frac{\text{R{=A}}}{{=ds}}$
Calculate and round to two decimal places: $P=\text{R{=fixed(P, 2)}}$
notes: Harder variant built on the two twists of ex9-7-3 (R50000, 8.5 %, ages 13 to 18 gives R35087.72 when w = 8, a1 = 13, g = 5, k = 50): the number of years is not given and must be found from two ages, and the rate has a half-percent so i has three decimal places and the divisor 1 + in is a three-decimal number. The rate is always x.5 % so i prints exactly as 0.0w5. Ages stay at most 20. The requires keep P a non-integer and away from an exact half-cent tie (a tie occurs only when 200000A/th is an odd integer). Numeric family, so no distractors and no misconception ids.
